Issued at 105 AM CDT Tue Oct 27 2026

As of 1am, radar indicates light rain showers mainly along and east 
of the James River (with the bulk of it over east central SD) as 
temps remain above freezing, in the upper 30s. The wrap around 
portion, that we saw as snow earlier, has now moved off into ND/MN, 
but there is still the potential for light flurries lingering over 
north central to the James River, mainly along the ND/SD border. 
Winds are out of the northeast between 10-15 mph with visibilities 
down to 5-6SM at KABR and KATY and down to 7SM at KMBG.

CAMs/REFS/NBM overall agree on the last of the precip exiting 
NESD/MN by ~12Z or so. By this time, its negatively tilted upper 
wave's axis will be over eastern ND through MN and clipping far NESD 
and its nearly stacked surface low hovering over southwestern/south 
central MN and SD border. Through the morning this entire system 
will continue to track off towards the northeast. However, REFs/NBM 
indicates low stratus clouds/fog will be hanging around through much 
of the morning before starting to clear out over south central SD 
midday or so. These clouds will somewhat clear across central and 
potentially portions of NESD/MN this evening through the early parts 
of tonight. With these low clouds/moisture, soundings do indicate we 
could be dealing with ongoing drizzle (maybe light freezing drizzle 
over north central for the next couple of hours) given the classic 
drizzle sounding, with a saturated layer from the surface to about 
900mb/lift and dry air right above it. Latest obs back this up with 
ceilings only 500-600ft. As these lower clouds move out (and 
ceilings improve)this will end the drizzle threat, however, with
the clouds hanging over NESD/MN this could continue the drizzle
threat well through the afternoon, as soundings suggest. So I 
did add drizzle mention into the grids until 15Z for now. Less 
confidence beyond this time but may need to be extending over 
our eastern CWA.

As winds become light tonight, mainly out of the south, with the 
saturated grounds combining with radiational cooling, the potential 
for fog/drizzle is looking possible and potentially could be 
widespread. NAM soundings across the entire CWA show some lift in 
the saturated lower levels at ~900mb and below. REFS backs this
up, leading to higher confidence, as it indicates widespread 
low clouds, in the form of fog, forming over central SD 
overnight and potentially spreading across NESD/MN through 
Wednesday morning. It could be dense as REFS/HREF probability of
visibility (by 12Z Wednesday) at 1/4th mile or less is up to 
50-80% with these higher values between the Mo and James River.
However NBM says 15% or less. Latest run of the ConsShort does 
in fact show viz tanking lowest over this location. The only 
thing that could hamper this is if lower clouds move back in 
quicker with this next system or there is less low level 
saturation aka dewpoint depression is higher. So a Fog Headline 
may be needed, especially for areas between the Mo and James 
River, as the next shift can look at this. 

Through Wednesday aloft, the region will be in west to southwest 
flow as a large closed mid level low will track southeastward and 
over western Canada. With this, a couple of shortwaves will spin 
cyclonically around the low with the first one clipping northwestern 
SD/western ND/MT this afternoon and the other one tracking 
northeastward across the Dakotas tonight through Wednesday 
afternoon. The first wave and its surface low will keep any precip 
chances to the northwest and north of the CWA. With the Wednesday 
wave and its low/cold front, precipitation chances return. The 
highest pops of 60-85% will be ahead of the cold front James 
Valley and eastward with the highest pops of 70%+ Coteau and 
eastward with south to southwest flow ushering in moisture 
combining with daytime heating and lift from the front. Models 
suggest even some marginal CAPE for thunderstorms! By the 
evening, the entire CWA will be behind the front with dry 
weather forecast Thursday through Friday as a high will be 
dominant over the area. Any shift in the low's track or timing 
will result in a change to pops. Luckily Ptype will be all rain 
a highs will be in the 50s to the lower 60s. Precip chances look
to return Friday night through the weekend. Aloft will consist 
of a -PNA setup as a ridge will build over the region 
Friday/Saturday before tracking eastward as the trough over the 
western CONUS tracks east.

Highs for today will range in the mid 40s to the lower 60s, warmest 
over south central SD with overnight lows in the 30s to around 40. 
However, confidence remains lower on how warm we will get today as 
the NBM 25-75th spread is 4-7 degrees due to the clouds and how fast 
they can clear out by peak heating. Same for Wednesday with the 
clouds, with a spread of 5-8 degrees. Through the end of the 
week, temps will remain normal to slightly above normal with
